form.label: Kong Proxy - Latency Analysis
form.description: Where request time is actually spent. Separates Kong's own overhead from upstream wait, so a slowdown can be attributed to a plugin rather than blamed on the backend. All upstream statistics exclude short-circuited requests.

search.query: `kong_base` | stats count by service | sort - count

html.div: Reading these panels on Kong 3.4. latencies.kong on 3.4 is Kong's plugin and routing overhead plus request receive time, added together in the serializer. Kong 3.5 splits receive time into its own field, so every threshold on this dashboard shifts on upgrade. latencies.proxy is time waiting on the upstream, and -1 means the request never got there - those are excluded here, not treated as zero.

search.query: `kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | stats p95(total_ms) as v | eval v=round(v,0)
`kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | stats p95(proxy_ms) as v | eval v=round(v,0)
`kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | stats p95(kong_ms) as v | eval v=round(v,0)
`kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | stats p99(proxy_ms) as v | eval v=round(v,0)
`kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | stats max(total_ms) as v | eval v=round(v,0)
`kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | timechart span=$span$ p50(proxy_ms) as p50, p90(proxy_ms) as p90, p95(proxy_ms) as p95, p99(proxy_ms) as p99, max(proxy_ms) as max

html.p: If the red band grows while the blue stays flat, the problem is inside Kong - a plugin, the datastore, or DNS - not the backend.

search.query: `kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | timechart span=$span$ p95(kong_ms) as "Kong overhead p95", p95(proxy_ms) as "Upstream wait p95"

`kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | eval bucket=case(proxy_ms<10,"1: <10ms", proxy_ms<50,"2: 10-50ms", proxy_ms<100,"3: 50-100ms", proxy_ms<250,"4: 100-250ms", proxy_ms<500,"5: 250-500ms", proxy_ms<1000,"6: 0.5-1s", proxy_ms<5000,"7: 1-5s", proxy_ms<30000,"8: 5-30s", true(),"9: >30s") | stats count by bucket | sort bucket

html.p: The Kong service config sets read_timeout to 60000 ms. Requests crossing 80% of that (48000 ms) are about to become 504s. This panel is the leading indicator for that alert.

search.query: `kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | eval near_timeout = if(proxy_ms >= (`kong_read_timeout_ms` * 0.8), 1, 0) | timechart span=$span$ sum(near_timeout) as "Within 80% of timeout", count as "Total requests"

`kong_proxied` | search $svc$ | stats count as requests, p50(proxy_ms) as p50_ms, p95(proxy_ms) as p95_ms, p99(proxy_ms) as p99_ms, max(proxy_ms) as max_ms, avg(kong_ms) as avg_kong_ms by service, route, upstream_path | where requests >= 10 | eval p50_ms=round(p50_ms,0), p95_ms=round(p95_ms,0), p99_ms=round(p99_ms,0), max_ms=round(max_ms,0), avg_kong_ms=round(avg_kong_ms,1) | sort - p95_ms | head 25

panel.title: Kong overhead by route - plugin cost

html.p: Routes with elevated Kong overhead are running more or slower plugins. ee-smp-functests carries the rate-limiting plugin, so a rise there may mean the limiter's datastore is slow.

search.query: `kong_base` | search $svc$ | stats count as requests, p50(kong_ms) as p50_kong_ms, p95(kong_ms) as p95_kong_ms, max(kong_ms) as max_kong_ms by service, route | eval p50_kong_ms=round(p50_kong_ms,1), p95_kong_ms=round(p95_kong_ms,1), max_kong_ms=round(max_kong_ms,1) | sort - p95_kong_ms
